sets.title: Scope-owned child tasks and cooperative cancellation

objective_text.T73.01.a: Explain scope-owned task lifetime, failure aggregation and cooperative cancellation, including why a cancellation flag does not establish completion or a bounded join latency.
objective_text.T73.01.b: Derive admission/closing/quiescent states, implement spawn/join and deterministic error selection, then compose with the existing work.pool artifact without detached tasks or prematurely released contexts.
objective_text.T73.01.c: Inject failure before every admission, record thread/context ownership, join zero/one/eight children, reject ninth admission and late spawn. Use a barrier-controlled failure with siblings acknowledging cancellation and compare accepted/completed counts. Reject both missing-cancellation and swallowed-result mutants. Run separate TSan and demonstrate that eventual cancellation needs child checkpoints.
objective_text.T73.01.d: Add nested nurseries with a parent deadline: propagate cancellation down while joining upward, retaining contexts until every descendant is quiescent. Delayed assessment supplies two failures racing in different orders; keep deterministic creation-order reporting while preserving both errors in a bounded aggregate.

sets.title: Bounded CSP channels, rendezvous and atomic select

objective_text.T73.02.a: Derive readiness, linearization, close/drain and cancellation semantics; compare deterministic selection with Go ready-case randomness and distinguish rendezvous acknowledgment from merely enqueuing an offer.
objective_text.T73.02.b: Implement buffered/rendezvous operations and select with a single predicate-registration boundary, explicit spurious-wakeup loops, finite tickets and quiescent destruction; retain coroutine frames until generation-specific disarm.
objective_text.T73.02.c: Test full/empty, both ready, one closed, all closed, close with buffered values, cancellation with blocked sender/receiver and accepted-versus-unaccepted rendezvous. Repeatedly inject spurious broadcasts. Capture event histories and verify no lost/duplicated accepted values. Reject send-after-close and skipped-buffer mutants; independently model sequential traces and use TSan for actual threads.
objective_text.T73.02.d: Change unsigned copies to owned buffers with a destructor: define ownership on failed send, close/drain and cancellation. Delayed assessment splits the hub into separately locked channels; derive a registration/recheck protocol that prevents a wakeup lost between observing empty and going to sleep, or justify retaining the common lock.

objective_text.T73.03.a: Separate sender recipe, connected operation storage, start permission and completion ownership; identify the dated C++ proposal guarantees that an exposed C struct does not enforce.
objective_text.T73.03.b: Implement the serialized state protocol and backend lifetime adapter, including synchronous completion, cancellation races, callback reentrancy policy and exactly-once terminal release.
objective_text.T73.03.c: Enumerate invalid start/complete orders, value/error/stopped alternatives and cancellation-before-completion. Use a receiver that frees a heap state to detect post-callback access under ASan. Reject duplicate-completion and cancel-as-completion mutants. For a concurrent adapter, use one atomic winner and demonstrate that losers never inspect reclaimed storage without their own retained reference.
objective_text.T73.03.d: Allow an operation to complete inline during start and let the receiver destroy its enclosing object. Delayed assessment connects a chain of two operations; ensure the successor starts only after ownership transfers and no predecessor field is accessed after its receiver may have destroyed it.

objective_text.T73.04.a: Explain mailbox ownership, actor identity across restart, run-to-completion serialization and the limit of let-it-crash recovery when effects have already escaped the actor.
objective_text.T73.04.b: Implement admission, dispatch, death and reincarnation with finite generation retirement; design the channel-to-actor executor boundary and message-drop ownership.
objective_text.T73.04.c: Test full mailbox, stale identity, nested step, failure with queued work, restart while alive and generation exhaustion. Reject stale-generation admission and retained-dead-mailbox mutants. Record effects before failure to show they are not rolled back. Compare actor serialization to a mutex-protected shared object under the same observable ordering.

sets.title: Multiversion visibility, reader pins and bounded reclamation

objective_text.T73.08.a: Derive version visibility and retention from reader lifetimes, distinguish repeatable snapshot reads from stronger isolation, and identify how a forgotten pin creates resource retention.
objective_text.T73.08.b: Implement timestamped publication, exact pin identity, visible-version selection and reclamation with a bounded-space proof under the four-reader assumption.
objective_text.T73.08.c: Enumerate pin/publish/read/drop traces against an independent immutable-history model, test four pins at different versions and a fifth refusal, stale slot reuse and generation retirement. Reject pin-ignorant collection and missing-generation mutants. Track retained version counts before/after releases and compare the mutex cost with read-copy-update assumptions.
objective_text.T73.08.d: Give each version separately owned payload storage whose clone can fail; publish only after full construction and preserve old readers on failure. Delayed assessment adds independent keys and predicate queries: construct write skew under snapshot isolation and explain what validation or locking would establish the stronger requested property.

sets.title: Sequence validation without racing ordinary C payloads

objective_text.T73.09.a: Separate storage race freedom, coherent snapshot validation, writer serialization, retry bounds and counter lifetime; identify what SC proves and what a later weakened implementation must re-establish.
objective_text.T73.09.b: Derive the atomic representation and SC ordering argument, implement bounded retry and nonwrapping writer publication, and account for every output and failure effect.
objective_text.T73.09.c: Test odd/even transitions, zero retry, interrupted writer state, output canaries and counter exhaustion. Reject odd-sequence acceptance and omitted-payload-write mutants. Run actual concurrent stress and TSan while explaining that clean runs do not prove weak-order correctness. Inspect disassembly and compare lock-free status and fences with an equivalent mutex snapshot.
objective_text.T73.09.d: Derive a weaker-order version from explicit synchronization/fence reasoning and check it with a C memory-model tool before comparing costs. Delayed assessment uses pointer payloads and a reader that pauses after loading one pointer; add lifetime protection or reject the design, since sequence validation does not retain pointees.

sets.title: Demand signaling, terminal events and bounded reentrancy

objective_text.T73.10.a: Derive demand accounting, signal ordering, cancellation and reentrancy limits; compare the original C subset to selected Reactive Streams rules without claiming interface or certification equivalence.
objective_text.T73.10.b: Implement explicit demand/terminal/delivering state, saturating unbounded arithmetic and callback ownership; construct a channel adapter that never delivers more items than requested.
objective_text.T73.10.c: Enumerate request/emit/cancel/end traces, test zero and maximum demand, callback requests/cancellation and recursive emission. Reject emission without credit and repeated-terminal mutants. Independently account for requested versus delivered finite items, retain callback context through return and test that end requires no demand.
objective_text.T73.10.d: Make signals originate on several threads: serialize them through one executor and retain the subscription until all in-flight signals quiesce. Delayed assessment introduces a slow subscriber and bounded channel capacity; compare blocking, dropping and failure policies under the same stated delivery contract, with T75 owning the overload decision.

variants.prompt: Emit with demand0 is EMPTY. Request1 then emit99 whose callback requests1 leaves demand1 without recursive delivery; emit7 consumes it. UINT64_MAX then request1 stays unbounded. Complete then error produces one terminal event; later emit is CLOSED. Cancellation prevents subsequent emits but does not establish cross-thread callback quiescence. Derive each transition before executing.
